messages:
Alex: quick heads up — customer on prod is seeing SSE streams drop after ~30s and getting partial outputs. repro from their side: they get a few events then stream closes with HTTP 200 but incomplete event data.
Maria: which infra in front of us? ALB/cloudflare/envoy? any proxies?
Alex: path: Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx reverse proxy -> redwood-hosted runtime (http/1.1).
Samir: common culprits: proxy buffering + idle timeouts + half-close on backend. do we have nginx set to proxy_buffering on by default?
Ingrid: yep default is on. also ALB idle timeout is 60s, Cloudflare keeps its own idle window. But customer reports it happens much earlier (~25-35s).
Maria: can we get connection-level logs from the runtime when it closes? any FIN/RST?
Alex: attached logs from runtime socket layer show graceful half-close from upstream, then client-side reads EOF shortly after. snippet:

```
[INFO] conn=0x7f9a2 stream_id=1234: received last_chunk, keep-alive pending
[INFO] conn=0x7f9a2 stream_id=1234: write 512 bytes, flushed
[WARN] conn=0x7f9a2 stream_id=1234: downstream closed half (SOCKET_SHUT_WR)
[INFO] conn=0x7f9a2 stream_id=1234: connection closed by peer
```

Samir: sounds like upstream (nginx or ALB) is doing a half-close after finishing chunk because it's coalescing chunks. If proxy_buffering is on, nginx will buffer until buffer full or connection ends, then send and close. For SSE we need immediate flush and keep connection open.
Ingrid: did customer mention any intermediary CDN keepalive settings? Cloudflare sometimes enforces its own 100s but also has websocket fallback behaviours. they said they were on Cloudflare Spectrum.
Maria: repro steps requested. Alex can you paste minimal curl that reproduces?
Alex: customer was using JS EventSource in browser and also a simple curl -N which triggers it too. Repro command: `curl -v -N 'https://example.com/v1/streams?model=...&client=abc'` and will see initial data events then connection ends with no `event: close` etc.
Samir: try curl with --http1.1 and add `-H 'Connection: keep-alive'` and `-H 'Accept: text/event-stream'` to force not to negotiate http2. Also test `curl -v --no-buffer` (`-N` is alias) and `stdbuf -oL` in case local buffer.
Ingrid: from nginx side, suggested config to fix SSE:

```
location /v1/streams/ {
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Connection "";    # preserve chunked
    proxy_buffering off;                 # stream immediately
    proxy_cache off;
    proxy_read_timeout 300s;            # allow long-lived
    send_timeout 300s;
}
```

Maria: and for ALB: increase idle timeout to > client read timeout (e.g., 300s). Also ensure target group has deregistration delay etc.
Samir: add to that: at OS/TCP layer, disable Nagle (set tcp_nodelay) helps small writes flush immediately. Nginx directive `proxy_socket_keepalive on;` and use `tcp_nodelay on;` for upstream. For Envoy: use `streaming_filters` and `proxy_buffer_limit` toggles. Example envoy snippet:

```
- name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
    stream_idle_timeout: 0s  # disable envoys own idle close
    common_http_protocol_options:
      idle_timeout: 0s
```

Samir: important: setting idle_timeout to 0s disables idle close for long-lived streams. But be careful for resource leaks.
Alex: customer also saw partial event payloads — like half a JSON object: {"text":"This is a... then connection death. Could be chunk fragmentation + connection close mid-chunk.
Maria: any Cloudflare-specific notes?
Ingrid: Cloudflare will buffer for certain response types and may close early on connectivity gating for non-websocket long polling. For Stream/SSE we often recommend Cloudflare page rules to bypass cache and use `cache: bypass` and `origin keep-alive` settings, or use a Cloudflare Argo tunnel. Also `CF-Worker` proxied responses sometimes rewrite headers.
Samir: add header recommendations: `Cache-Control: no-transform, no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx to signal no buffering. Some proxies respect `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
Alex: I pushed a quick patch to the customer's nginx upstream: disabled proxy_buffering and increased proxy_read_timeout, then they reported streams stayed alive. But they later saw intermittent early closes.
Maria: what about ALB and connection reuse? ALB will reuse backend connections and may half-close the TCP if it thinks request done. For SSE keep connection per request open; set keepalive on backend and higher max for target group. Also ensure ALB has `connection: keep-alive` to origin.
Ingrid: Also check the client's browser. Some mobile browsers will suspend background tabs and close connections prematurely. we should confirm customer was testing in foreground.
Alex: they were. Also repro from their server side curl happened too.
Samir: next steps for triage: 1) collect full tcpdump from the ALB-target interface (or just from nginx host) to see FIN/RST sequence; 2) reproduce with curl -v -N against origin (bypass cloudflare if possible); 3) test toggling `proxy_buffering off` and `tcp_nodelay on`; 4) increase ALB idle timeout to >300s and set nginx `proxy_read_timeout` accordingly; 5) if using Envoy, disable stream_idle_timeout and set idle timeout 0s.
Maria: I'll email the customer the repro checklist and proposed changes. include a code snippet they can drop into nginx. Also offer a brief window to pair on tcpdump.
Alex: doing tcpdump now — will paste pcap link when done. quick note: saw `SYN,ACK` then `FIN` from ALB side shortly after last chunk — looks like ALB closed because it thought backend finished response.
Ingrid: could be backend returning `Content-Length` accidentally. If response has Content-Length header, proxies may consider it complete. Ensure SSE endpoints do not set Content-Length and use `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` or none for streaming.
Samir: yes — double-check the runtime is not setting Content-Length for streaming responses. Also avoid `Connection: close` header.
ops-bot: Incident tracker created: INC-2026, assigned to @Alex, priority P2.
Maria: thanks all. Alex please update thread after tcpdump and config changes. I'll follow up with customer later today. :thumbsup:
